content_of_post_to_comment:
In the past, I spent a lot of time on social media. I checked my phone as soon as I woke up, before studying, and even before going to bed. I often watched short videos, read posts, and scrolled through my feed for hours without realizing how much time had passed.

After a while, I noticed that this habit was affecting my daily life. I found it harder to concentrate on my studies, often procrastinated, and spent less time with my family. I also felt tired because I was looking at my phone screen too often.

Because of this, I decided to reduce my social media use. I started setting a daily time limit, turning off unnecessary notifications, and avoiding social media while studying or before going to sleep. Instead, I spent my free time reading books, exercising, and doing other productive activities.

Although it was not easy at first, I gradually noticed many positive changes. I became more focused, more productive, and slept better. I also had more time to improve myself and enjoy real-life activities. I realized that I did not need to keep up with everything happening on social media.

For me, reducing social media use does not mean quitting it completely. Social media is still useful for communication and getting information. However, it should be used wisely so that it does not take control of our time and daily lives. By using social media in a balanced way, we can enjoy both the digital world and real life.
comment: The part about not quitting social media completely is something I think a lot of people miss. It’s usually not the apps themselves but the automatic checking that steals time. I found that replacing the habit with something specific, like reading a few pages or taking a walk when I wanted to scroll, worked better than just trying to use willpower.
